# PR #248 performance review — PASS WITH NOTES

Head: 2bfd4dcbb779a4847b07738d772ba0c9686e741e
Reviewer: pij-vast-silkworm, role performance/248
Request: 01a1f15f-de11-7601-b061-30a97070c316
Scope: launch cost, in-process scaling, spawn accounting, CI evidence and live pre-deploy baseline. Correctness/security verdicts remain with their assigned reviewers. No local cargo build/test or daemon bounce performed.

## Decision

No blocking performance finding. The normal main-checkout, linked-worktree and non-repository paths launch nothing, including their first observation. Unknown layouts retain the existing git launch site, guarded by a 600-second per-folder answer cache. This removes a boot/new-folder burst, not a previous one-git-per-seat-per-minute steady-state rate. Source review is inferential; the CI launch-counter test is deterministic. Candidate behavior on the live macOS fleet is not yet measured.

Placement is POLICY: the returned repository key selects the PA/prime scope; it is not a one-directional brake.

## Cost and scaling

- Existing scheduler only: TICK=60 seconds; one owned watchdog instance, serialized awaited rounds. No new timer, poll, task, process launch site or per-tick-per-seat launch.
- Before: one git per distinct placed folder per daemon lifetime, plus each new folder; unplaceable folders retried once per 600 seconds. PR historical receipts 23 at uptime 6min -> 23 at 7m39s -> 25 at 13m47s are reported by the author, not independently re-created here.
- After normal placement: zero git launches at boot and steady state. A directory walk performs metadata checks per ancestor; a worktree/submodule-style pointer adds two read_to_string calls and canonicalization. These calls use ordinary git metadata; the code does not enforce a small-file byte limit.
- After fallback: at most one git invocation per Unknown folder per 600 seconds in the serialized watchdog, including cached success or failure; average <=U/600 invocations/s for U continuously Unknown folders, with an initial U-folder burst. Git has the existing 2-second timeout and kill_on_drop. root::place runs before cache lookup, so a readable replacement bypasses an old fallback answer immediately. No recursive pointer traversal: at most one gitdir pointer and one commondir are read.
- Important documentation precision: filesystem placement is NOT once per distinct folder per round. For N live seats and P watched PAs, scope_of performs N+1 repo calls per PA (pa_watchdog.rs:514-515,976-985), then presence_scopes performs N more calls (pa_presence.rs:274-276), plus tombstoned-parent anchors. The quiet path is approximately P*(N+1)+N walks per 60-second round: O((P+1)*N*D) metadata work at ancestor depth D. Same-folder seats repeat the walk. Limit wakes and dormant notifications can add scope walks; last_pa scans tombstoned PAs only on a would-be missing-PA send and launches nothing. The docs' per-call description is true, but the per-PA multiplier should remain visible when judging cost.
- Fallback launch is still spawns::record("git.pa-watchdog-common-dir") immediately before program::launch_async("git", ...), not a shell. The resolver caches a PATH hit; the normal installed git path is absolute. It is the existing launch, not an added site. spawn_sites.rs scans daemon production Command builders for accounting and separately trips over bare git/tmux launches. It is a source tripwire, not complete runtime proof.
